 Sajid Raza Published: Oct 22, 2026, 16:43 IST Updated: Oct 22, 2026, 16:43 IST When is Diwali 2026? Will schools be closed on Monday? Diwali 2026 will be celebrated on Sunday, November 8 , across most parts of India. Also known as Deepavali, the festival is one of the most important Hindu festivals and is celebrated with prayers, lights, sweets and family gatherings.
 With Diwali being celebrated on a Sunday this year, students and parents might be asking themselves whether the schools will be closed on Monday 9th November. Govardhan Puja will be celebrated on the next day after Diwali and it is a public holiday or School holiday in some states including Uttar Pradesh. School holiday programs may change depending on the State, School Board and individual school, however.
 Diwali is also known as Chhoti Diwali, Govardhan Puja and Bhai Dooj. 
 Please refer to each school's calendar for specific dates of the festive break and classes reopening.
 Will schools be closed on monday, november 9?
 Schools may remain closed on Monday, November 9, 2026, for Govardhan Puja, particularly in states where the festival is an official school holiday.
 Govardhan Puja is a part of the festive calendar of Uttar Pradesh state. Schools on the state holiday calendar may be closed on this day. Final decision is based on the official school calendar and local education department directions.
 The day may be a regular working day in other states. Other schools (private, central, and state government schools) can have different holiday schedules.
 It is recommended that parents and students consult the current notice that was issued by their school before making plans.
 Diwali 2026 full festival calendar: Important dates
 The Diwali festival is celebrated over several days, with each day having its own religious and cultural significance. Here are the key dates to remember in 2026.
 Festival Date Day 
 Dhanteras November 6, 2026 Friday 
 Chhoti Diwali / Naraka Chaturdashi November 8, 2026 Sunday 
 Diwali / Deepavali November 8, 2026 Sunday 
 Govardhan Puja November 9, 2026 Monday 
 Bhai Dooj November 11, 2026 Wednesday 
 Note: Festival dates and observances may vary by regional calendar and local religious traditions. Check a local panchang for the precise date and puja timings.
 Govardhan puja 2026: Date and significance 
 Govardhan Puja will be observed on Monday, November 9, 2026. The festival is celebrated on the day after Diwali in many parts of India, although the exact observance can vary according to regional traditions.
 Govardhan Puja is related to Lord Krishna and Govardhan Hill. 
 The Hindu belief is that Lord Krishna lifted this hill to save the people of Vrindavan from the heavy rain that Lord Indra had sent.
 On this day, the people worship Govardhan Hill and prepare special food offering called Annakut. The festival is especially celebrated in Uttar Pradesh, especially in the Braj region, such as Mathura and Vrindavan.
 For students, November 9 may be a school holiday in states where Govardhan Puja is officially observed.
 Bhai dooj 2026: When will it be celebrated?
 Bhai Dooj will be celebrated on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. The festival is a celebration of the relationship between brothers and sisters and is celebrated on the second day after Diwali in numerous regional traditions.
 Sisters put tilak on brothers' forehead on Bhai Dooj and pray for their long life, happiness and well-being. Usually, brothers exchange gifts with their sisters to demonstrate their love for them.
 The festival is also called Bhai Tika or Bhau Beej in other parts of the country. It is an important family event in some parts of India and may form part of the school break.
 The decision on whether schools will be closed on November 11 will be subject to the appropriate state holiday calendar and the individual school.
 How long will the Diwali school holidays last in 2026?
 The duration of the Diwali school holidays will differ across India. Some schools may provide only the officially declared festival holidays, while others may announce a break of several days.
 In states such as Uttar Pradesh, the festive period may include Diwali and Govardhan Puja, with Bhai Dooj also appearing in the state holiday calendar. Schools may follow different schedules depending on their management and academic requirements.
 Students should keep the following points in mind:
 Sunday, November 8: Diwali falls on a Sunday.
 Monday, November 9: Govardhan Puja may be a school holiday in several states.
 Wednesday, November 11: Bhai Dooj may be a holiday in states where it is officially observed.
 School reopening: The date will depend on the institution's declared festive break.
 There is no single nationwide school holiday schedule covering every day of the Diwali festival. Students should rely on official school announcements rather than assume that all schools will remain closed throughout the festive period.
